Securities and Futures Ordinance; relevant regulated-activity definitions and licensing provisions

evidence.quote: these FAQs seek to provide additional guidance on the implications of the licensing regime under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (the “Ordinance”) to single family offices and multi-family offices.

claims.statement: The FAQs provide additional guidance under the Ordinance for both single family offices and multi-family offices.

evidence.quote: No, the Ordinance does not define “family” or “family office”.

claims.statement: The source states that the Ordinance defines neither “family” nor “family office”.

claims.action: Determine licensing applicability independently of the family-office label

evidence.quote: the licensing regime does not hinge on whether an entity is called a family office or whether its clients are families.

claims.statement: Whether an entity is called a family office does not determine licensing applicability.

claims.action: Determine licensing obligations independently of clients’ family status

evidence.quote: the licensing regime does not hinge on whether an entity is called a family office or whether its clients are families.
the licensing obligations under the Ordinance do not hinge on whether the clients of a family office are family members or not.

claims.action: Determine legal form and operational structure
conditions: With respect to the services to be provided

evidence.quote: A family office operator will have more flexibility to determine its legal form and operational structure with respect to its services to be provided.

claims.statement: The source describes flexibility in selecting a family office’s legal form and operational structure for its intended services.
uncertainty: The extent of that flexibility is not specified; this is not an express licensing exemption.

claims.action: Manage the assets, investments and long-term interests of members of one family
conditions: For the purposes of the Circular

evidence.quote: What constitutes a single family office for the purposes of the Circular?

It typically refers to an arrangement (often structured through a corporate vehicle owned or controlled by the family) under which the assets, investments and long-term interests of members of a single family are managed.

claims.statement: For the Circular, a single family office typically means an arrangement managing one family’s assets, investments and long-term interests, often through a family-owned or family-controlled corporate vehicle.
uncertainty: “Typically” and “often” describe common arrangements, not mandatory structural conditions.

evidence.quote: The SFC has not sought to define what relationships of blood or of law would constitute family membership

claims.statement: The SFC has not sought to define which blood or legal relationships constitute family membership.

claims.action: Assess the licensing obligation using three jointly required factors
conditions: Its services constitute one or more regulated activities as defined under the Ordinance
It carries on a business providing those services
That business is carried on in Hong Kong

claims.statement: Q3 states a conjunctive licensing trigger: all three factors must be present for a single family office’s licensing obligation to arise.

evidence.quote: secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services;

claims.statement: The second factor requires carrying on a business in the provision of those services.
